answer: Co-located Hardware Attestation. Each agent identity must present a signed boot measurement from a tamper-resistant chip bound to its host, and the registry rejects any two identities whose attestations share a physical die. An attacker therefore cannot multiply identities without buying distinct physical devices. Spawning a thousand agents costs a thousand chips, a meadow of hardware rather than a line of code. Operators who reach the summit of scale must sustain real per-unit procurement and maintenance, and a single machine at any umber hour yields exactly one identity.
